papers.title: New traversable wormholes without invoking exotic matter in $f(Q)$ from the freedom of different connections
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wormhole solutions in General Relativity can only exist in the presence of exotic matter that violates the null energy condition. In this paper, we investigate the possibility of constructing wormhole solutions in $f(Q)$ gravity in which the extra connection degrees of freedom contribute such that no exotic matter is needed. Considering the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole as an example, we find that the system admits two families of connections consistent with the spacetime symmetries and the requirements of symmetric teleparallel gravity. For both families, we show that constant non-metricity scalar $Q$ is not merely a simplifying assumption but arises naturally from the field equations when $f_{QQ}$ is regular, and that the resulting exact analytic solutions can satisfy the null energy condition throughout the entire spacetime. For the second family, which possesses richer connection degrees of freedom, we further demonstrate that solutions with a spatially varying $Q$ exist when $f_{QQ}$ is allowed to diverge at a finite value of $Q$, and that these too can satisfy the null energy condition everywhere. Our results show that the nontrivial connection degrees of freedom in $f(Q)$ gravity can naturally be responsible for supporting wormhole geometries, without resorting to any exotic matter.
papers.authors: Ismael Ayuso, Mariam Bouhmadi-L\'opez, Che-Yu Chen, Konstantinos Dialektopoulos

papers.title: Isomorphisms of Class S Theories with IndexLab
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use IndexLab to scan untwisted and twisted class $\mathcal{S}$ constructions based on ADE Lie algebras of rank up to seven, as well as $A_8$ and $E_8$. We consider surfaces of genus at most three with up to five punctures, covering 167,244,647 constructions in total. To find candidate pairs of isomorphic theories, we compare Schur and Hall-Littlewood indices, Weyl anomalies, Coulomb branch spectra, and flavor data. We set aside pairs explained by known mechanisms, leaving a catalogue of 5,278 candidate pairs. Recurring changes in rank, puncture labels, and twists suggest families of candidate isomorphisms. We group 99.58% of the pairs into 25 families and 6 finite families. IndexLab is available at superconformal.com.
papers.authors: Zhihao Duan, Zhenghao Zhong

papers.title: Hidden wormholes from an action principle in $D=4$
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present new black hole solutions for the class of gravitational effective field theories in four spacetime dimensions that extend General Relativity while retaining the graviton as the only degree of freedom of gravitational origin. We consider terms up to cubic order in curvature, solve the resulting field equations, and find one-way hidden wormholes as numerical solutions: these are regular black holes with an interior wormhole throat that is crossable in one direction and leads to a cosmological spacetime in its interior. They are regular and have no inner horizon, thus evading the mass inflation instability that afflicts conventional regular black hole geometries.
papers.authors: Francesco Del Porro, Alessia Platania, Samuele Silveravalle

papers.title: An infrared-safe $S$-matrix for $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scattering amplitudes of massless gauge theories are not observables: they are infrared divergent, and the standard regulators are tied either to perturbation theory or the planar limit. We study $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory on rigid AdS$_4$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the role of the amplitude is played by correlation functions of boundary operators. These are finite, and they are defined at any coupling and for any gauge group. Among them, the four-point function of the flavor-current supermultiplet is the counterpart of the $2\to2$ amplitude of the elementary supergluon states, and arguably the simplest non-trivial observable of the theory. In this paper, we compute it at weak coupling to one loop. The tree-level correlator follows directly from the microscopic theory, and the one-loop correlator, which we obtain from AdS unitarity, takes a remarkably simple form in Mellin space. In the flat-space limit, it reproduces the one-loop scattering amplitude, with the infrared divergences re-emerging as logarithms.
papers.authors: Maria Nocchi, Leonardo Rastelli

papers.title: 'Forward-backward' flows and integration cycles for semiclassical Euclidean gravity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrating Euclidean semiclassical gravity over real Riemannian metrics is subtle due to the conformal factor problem. A perturbative prescription was given by Gibbons-Hawking-Perry (GHP) where the integration contour for the conformal perturbations is rotated to be imaginary. A potential non-perturbative remedy is that the integration cycles associated to semiclassical saddle points should be deformed into the space of complex metrics in the sense of Picard-Lefschetz theory. Here we propose a non-perturbative construction of such complex integration cycles. This employs a 'forward-backward' gradient flow of the Einstein-Hilbert action, starting at a saddle point, along which the action has monotonically increasing real part and constant imaginary part. The flow is not parabolic. In a neighbourhood of a saddle point, the real part of the conformal factor flows forward and that of the conformal class backwards, with the opposite true of their imaginary parts. Starting the flow at a saddle point, then roughly speaking, one specifies the real part of the conformal class and the imaginary part of the conformal factor at the end of the flow. Solving the flow one finds the complex metrics along a one parameter path within the integration cycle of that saddle, and varying this final data generates the integration cycle, the Lefschetz thimble of the saddle point. We find that near to a real saddle point this reproduces the GHP prescription. We characterise the neighbourhood of a saddle where such forward-backward flows may exist, finding a weaker restriction than that of Kontsevich-Segal-Witten. We numerically demonstrate flows explicitly for 4-dimensional gravity, constructing sections through the integration contours for the saddles given by Euclidean de Sitter, and for Schwarzschild in a cavity.
papers.authors: Nicholas M. K. Ross, Toby Wiseman

papers.title: Efficient and Optimal Analysis of Galaxy Surveys on Large Scales
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On sufficiently large scales the galaxy overdensity field is approximately Gaussian, so its information can be losslessly compressed into the power spectrum. Standard power spectrum estimators are nevertheless suboptimal on the largest scales, where the survey window induces significant coupling between different modes. Optimal power spectrum analysis typically requires an inverse of the covariance matrix, which can be overly expensive. Here we develop an alternative field level approach, which is significantly faster. We assess its impact on constraining primordial non-Gaussianity of the local type, which is particularly sensitive to these largest scales. Relative to the standard power spectrum analysis, our field level likelihood forecasts a $14\%$ improvement in constraining power. For the DESI DR2 LRG and QSO samples, our approach forecasts $\sigma(f_{\rm NL})=4.1$, compared to $\sigma(f_{\rm NL})=4.8$ from the power spectrum based analysis. The field level approach also enables efficient implementations of additional non-cosmological contributions to the signal. As an example, we present a novel non-parametric method to mitigate angular systematics, enabling efficient deprojection of contaminated modes.
papers.authors: Julius Adolff, Uro\v{s} Seljak

papers.title: Velocity Reconstruction from kSZ with SPT-3G and DESI-LS
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reconstruct the large-scale radial velocity field from the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect for the first time with the South Pole Telescope, and measure the galaxy-velocity correlation and the velocity power spectrum. We cross-correlate the SPT-3G D1 maps at 95, 150, and 220 GHz with luminous red galaxies from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys over the SPT-3G Main field. For the extended galaxy sample, we detect the galaxy-velocity correlation at signal-to-noise ratio $11.2$ and the velocity power spectrum at $8.1$, combining the three frequencies. We detect the reconstructed velocities for the first time at 220 GHz with signal-to-noise ratios of 4.2 and 3.1 from the galaxy-velocity correlation dipole and monopole, and at 3.8 from the velocity power spectrum. We model and estimate foreground contributions to the monopole, detecting both the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect and the cosmic infrared background contribution separately. On the around five percent of sky jointly covered by SPT-3G and DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, reconstructed velocities give new constraints on local-type primordial non-Gaussianity at $f_{\rm NL}=-38^{+61}_{-61}$, and adding galaxy clustering gives $f_{\rm NL}=-20^{+40}_{-46}$. The galaxy-velocity correlation is consistent between the three frequencies.
papers.authors: Selim C. Hotinli, Edmond Chaussidon, Simone Ferraro, Kendrick M. Smith

papers.title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.
papers.authors: Netta Engelhardt, Richard Nally

papers.title: Localization identities for spectral determinants: two-dimensional QCD and Ising field theory
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral determinants encode the meson spectra of planar two-dimensional QCD and of Ising field theory in the two-particle Bethe-Salpeter approximation. We derive localization identities for these determinants which express their logarithmic derivatives with respect to the spectral parameter in terms of Baxter $Q-$functions evaluated at special points, proving previously conjectured relations. Our derivation uses finite-rank commutation relations and virial identities of the underlying integral spectral operators. We identify a sufficient rational closure condition on the symbol of these operators that extends localization to a broader class of spectral problems and determines the evaluation points. Applications include generalized two-dimensional QCD with a quartic gauge-field potential and symbols interpolating between the QCD and Ising cases. We also give a general construction of the spectral operators and establish conditions for the finite-rank reduction on which localization relies.
papers.authors: Bercel Boldis, Nikolay Gromov, Gregory P. Korchemsky, Alessandro Testa

papers.title: All-Genus 2D $\mathcal{N}=1$ Superconformal Blocks
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a numerical algorithm for two dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks at arbitrary genera, in arbitrary plumbing channels, and for arbitrary spin structures. The algorithm utilizes two commuting copies of Virasoro subalgebras of the direct sum of the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal algebra with an auxiliary free fermion algebra, which allows us to reduce the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks to Virasoro conformal blocks.
papers.authors: Sam Christian, Yuchen Wang, Xi Yin, Yutai Zhang

papers.title: Not All Holographic Entropy Inequalities Are Free of Area Law Ultraviolet Divergences
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the AdS/CFT correspondence, linear constraints on subsystem entropies, which are necessary conditions for the validity of the Ryu-Takayanagi proposal, define the holographic entropy cone. We disprove a prior claim that all holographic constraints of this type are free of area law divergences (superbalanced). We analyze one explicit counterexample and explain how to easily find more; we report signatures of $\mathcal{O}(10^5)$ counterexamples. Our findings invalidate multiple prior claims and conjectures.
papers.authors: Xin-Xiang Ju, Bartlomiej Czech

papers.title: Supersymmetric warped AdS$_3$ solutions in eleven-dimensional supergravity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct new families of supersymmetric solutions of eleven-dimensional supergravity by deforming the half-BPS $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times \mathrm{S}^3_+\times \mathrm{S}^3_-\times\mathbb R^2$ background. We consider lightlike, spacelike and timelike warpings of the anti-de Sitter factor, accompanied by deformations of the two three-spheres, and determine the supporting four-form fluxes and the constraints imposed by the equations of motion. In particular, the deformation parameters of the two spheres are necessarily equal, although their radii need not coincide. We compute the conserved charges and determine the preserved supersymmetries and Killing superalgebras. Generic lightlike solutions preserve four real supercharges, whereas spacelike and timelike solutions preserve eight, with a Killing superalgebra containing a single exceptional $\mathfrak d(2,1;\alpha)$ factor.
papers.authors: Ruggero Noris

papers.title: Gravity/Thermodynamics Correspondence for Generic Dynamical Spacetimes
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Working within covariant phase space formalism, we establish \textit{gravity-thermodynamics correspondence} for generic dynamical spacetimes. We derive local first and second laws of thermodynamics on general null boundaries, for generic non-stationary solutions to Einstein gravity {with minimally coupled matter} for physical observers that we carefully specify. Entropy variation, which receives contribution only from the gravitational sector, is the surface charge variation associated with a vector field generating the null boundary, and temperature is its non-affinity parameter (divided by $2\pi$). The statement of the second law in our setting is that the entropy variation evaluated along the null vector field is strictly non-negative for the admissible positive-non-affinity clock and matter satisfying the null energy condition. Our dynamical entropy variation, which is non-integrable for generic non-stationary solutions, becomes integrable in near-stationary configurations, reproducing the Hollands--Wald--Zhang dynamical entropy formula. Strikingly, this local second law holds even when the boundary area is decreasing, disentangling thermodynamic irreversibility and the second law from standard area theorems. Our first-principles construction demonstrates that gravitational thermodynamics requires neither a stationary background, teleological event horizons, nor an exact entropy state function on individual codimension-1 spacelike slices of the null boundary (codimension two in spacetime).
papers.authors: Vahid Reza Shajiee, Mohammad Mehdi Sheikh-Jabbari, Vahid Taghiloo

papers.title: Baryonification V: Thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich maps from dark-matter-only lightcones
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Baryonic feedback is a major theoretical uncertainty for Stage-IV weak lensing (WL) surveys. The thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect traces the hot gas redistributed by feedback, so combining it with WL can calibrate feedback and improve cosmological constraints. Doing so with simulation-based inference requires correlated lensing and Compton-$y$ maps across many cosmologies and feedback scenarios. We present two methods to generate Compton-$y$ maps from dark-matter-only $N$-body light cones using the component-wise baryonification (BFC) model, which produces separate gas and stellar fields and computes the gas pressure from hydrostatic equilibrium. The two methods, painting pressure profiles onto halos or redistributing the signal along the baryonified gas, agree to within a few per cent. We calibrate the model to the fiducial and strongest AGN feedback FLAMINGO simulations by jointly fitting gas mass fractions and thermal pressure profiles, measuring the non-thermal pressure from the simulated gas velocities rather than treating it as a free parameter. The predicted Compton-$y$ profiles match FLAMINGO within halo-to-halo scatter, and when painted onto the FLAMINGO halos we reproduce the tSZ power spectrum of both feedback models to $\sim5\%$ for $500\lesssim\ell\lesssim3000$. Applied to a \emph{CosmoGridV1-like} $N$-body simulation, our maps agree with FLAMINGO within $\sim10\%$ for $300\lesssim\ell\lesssim8000$; the remaining differences come from the few hundred most massive clusters, and removing them from both halo catalogs brings the two into agreement. Our method thus enables accurate and efficient tSZ forward models from $N$-body simulation suites such as CosmoGridV1, an important step towards joint WL and tSZ simulation-based inference for Euclid, LSST, and the Simons Observatory.
papers.authors: Michael Kova\v{c}, Andrina Nicola, Jozef Bucko, Siyu Bian, Aurel Schneider, Robert Reischke, Jessica A. Cowell, Alexandre Refregier, Sambit K. Giri, Matthieu Schaller, Joop Schaye

papers.title: Cyclic Boson Stars with Quantum Vortex Molecules
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find a new type of stationary boson star with cyclic rotational symmetry in the minimal model of complex scalar field coupled to gravity. Unlike conventional axisymmetric spinning boson stars, these configurations can carry noninteger angular momentum per particle in units of the reduced Planck constant, revealing a new way for boson stars to carry angular momentum. We identify the vortex assemblies within these stars as self-gravitating quantum vortex molecules, in which gravity supports a stationary vortex arrangement despite internal circulation. These structures provide a relativistic realization of quantum vortex molecules studied in condensates and motivate possible laboratory analogues.
papers.authors: Xing-Yu Yang, Rong-Gen Cai

papers.title: Gravitational Mode Instabilities in Kerr-like Black Holes
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify exponentially growing modes of a homogeneous gravitational Teukolsky-like operator on highly spinning Kerr-like black holes subject to quasinormal mode boundary conditions. Specifically, we compute electromagnetic and gravitational quasinormal modes of a spacetime proposed by Konoplya, Rezzolla, and Zhidenko that parametrizes deformations from the Kerr geometry, including configurations with black hole spin parameter $a/M > 1$ that retain an event horizon. Using the continued fraction method, we find that the spin-weight $s=-2$ operator develops exponentially growing modes when the black hole spin and deformation parameters are sufficiently large, while the electromagnetic modes remain damped throughout the parameter space. We further compare the quasinormal mode predictions with an agnostic analysis of the GW250114 ringdown, identifying regions of the parameter space that are compatible with the spectrum inferred from the data.
papers.authors: Pedro Henrique Croti Siqueira, Rodrigo Dal Bosco Fontana, Maur\'icio Richartz

papers.title: Modular Hamiltonian and modular flow of a massive scalar in an interval
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain the vacuum modular Hamiltonian of a free massive scalar in an interval, for any $mL$. Its eigenvectors are superpositions of massive plane waves emitted from the two end points, with amplitudes given by a linear integral equation whose Neumann series is an expansion in reflections, and a normalization fixed by a Painlev\'e V transcendent. We follow the modular flow of initially localized wave packets inside the causal diamond. The flow is not geometric: the commutator profiles spread and can develop peaks ahead of the conformal trajectory.
papers.authors: Ra\'ul E. Arias, Daniel Fondevila

papers.title: Center anomalies without twists: torsion, exact degeneracies, and condensates
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed center anomalies are usually exposed by 't Hooft's twisted boundary conditions in a Hamiltonian formalism. On $\mathbb {RP}^3$, torsion makes the twist unnecessary: a center operator on the untwisted $SU(2)$ Hilbert space anticommutes with time reversal in Yang-Mills theory at $\theta=\pi$ and with the chiral symmetry of super Yang-Mills theory, so every level is at least doubly degenerate. The relevant semiclassical object is the BPST instanton, which descends to a charge-$\tfrac12$ saddle on the orbifold $\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2$. We complete it in two ways: applying a conformal transformation maps the orbifold to $\mathbb R\times\mathbb {RP}^3$, with the saddle describing the tunneling event between the two center sectors; by resolving the orbifold singularity, we obtain the Eguchi-Hanson space, which gives the gaugino condensate at its weak-coupling value.
papers.authors: Mohamed M. Anber

papers.title: Modular conjugations for thermal states and second worlds
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The modular conjugation $J$ maps an algebra of observables onto its commutant. For the vacuum on a Rindler wedge it is a spacetime reflection, but for thermal states in two-dimensional CFTs the known expressions involve chiral fields at the complex points $x\pm i\beta/2$, interpreted as belonging to a ``second world''. Here we compute $J$ for the geometric thermal state in explicit cyclic purifications, using either the vacuum vector, through the conformal map to a Rindler wedge, or a vector in the natural cone of a local algebra. The modular images are then fields at real points, and complex coordinates arise only when operators of the commutant outside the image of the thermal representation are written as fields on the original spacetime. For the chiral $U(1)$ current we also purify by doubling the Fock space, obtain explicit formulas for $J$, show that this purification coincides with Sorce's canonical purification, and treat all primary thermal states.
papers.authors: Alan Garbarz, Gabriel Palau, Guillem P\'erez-Nadal

papers.title: From Top to Bottom: Quark Mass Hierarchies in Heterotic String Theory
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard Model fermion masses exhibit large hierarchies, spanning more than five orders of magnitude in the quark sector alone. In this paper, we study whether these hierarchies can be generated perturbatively at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau compactifications, where the supergravity approximation remains under computational control. In such backgrounds, physical Yukawa couplings combine holomorphic superpotential integrals with matter field Kahler metrics. The former can be computed algebraically, while the latter require solving a coupled system of partial differential equations for the Ricci-flat metric, Hermitian Yang-Mills connections, and harmonic bundle-valued forms. Within this framework, we identify two new tree-level mechanisms by which complex structure moduli can generate fermion mass hierarchies and show analytically and numerically that both mechanisms are obstructed for previously studied tetra-quadric models. Motivated by these obstructions, we scan the existing databases of tens of thousands of complete intersection Calabi-Yau line bundle models and find a unique smooth quotient admitting a rank-three up-quark Yukawa matrix at tree level. Evaluating the physical couplings on this manifold and evolving them under the renormalization group, we obtain realistic mass hierarchies for the top, charm, up, and bottom quarks in the smooth supergravity regime.
papers.authors: Yuri Chervonyi, Fabian Ruehle, Nenad Tomasev

papers.title: Giant gravitons without giant gravitons
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that the partition function of a free bosonic $U(N)$ multi-matrix model admits a giant graviton expansion. For $d$ matrices, there are $d$ distinct giant gravitons, and the expansion can be characterized by a $d$-node quiver with bifundamentals connecting the nodes. This suggests the intriguing possibility of a more generalized holography where models without any obvious gravitational dual can nevertheless be given a dual brane interpretation. The giant graviton expansion of this multi-matrix model is somewhat unconventional though, as the giant graviton partition functions will necessarily have intrinsic $N$-dependence.
papers.authors: Blake J. Bottesi, James T. Liu

papers.title: The phase gradient spectrum: probing the squeezed bispectrum of the 21-cm signal during reionization
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The 21-cm signal from the epoch of reionization is highly non-Gaussian. Standard analyses rely on the power spectrum, which is blind to the Fourier phases, while higher-order statistics such as the bispectrum are computationally expensive and spread information across triangle configurations. As an efficient alternative, we develop the \textit{phase gradient spectrum}, which measures the circular coherence of phase differences between Fourier modes separated by a long-wavelength mode. We show analytically that this statistic measures the angle-averaged normalised squeezed bispectrum, which describes the response of small-scale power to long-wavelength fluctuations. Applied to reionization simulations with different ionizing source properties, the phase gradient spectrum of the 21-cm signal shows a characteristic non-monotonic evolution. At early times, the spectrum tracks the non-Gaussianity of the matter density field. Once the mean neutral fraction $\langle x_\mathrm{HI}\rangle \lesssim 0.9$, the spectrum follows the ionization topology. The phase coherence reaches a minimum midway through reionization and rises again as the remaining neutral regions shrink into isolated islands. Statistics that keep the sign of the squeezed bispectrum show that this minimum marks its sign change. This evolution holds for different reionization models and simulation frameworks. A Fisher forecast for a 1000-h Square Kilometre Array (SKA)-Low observation, combining five redshifts across reionization, shows that the phase gradient spectrum alone constrains the astrophysical parameters, and these constraints tighten by a factor of $\gtrsim 2$ for a 10,000-h observation. Combining the phase gradient spectrum with the power spectrum tightens the marginalised constraints by up to $\sim$20 per cent relative to the power spectrum alone.
papers.authors: Sambit K. Giri, P. Daniel Meerburg, L\'eon V. E. Koopmans

papers.title: Binary black-hole mergers with ultralight vector bosons
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We simulate the inspiral, merger, and ringdown of equal-mass, nonspinning binary black holes coupled to a massive vector (Proca) field. Starting from constraint-consistent electric-field initial data, we find that the Proca field rapidly concentrates around the black holes. However, it continues to exhibit nontrivial dynamics. Orbital evolution depends on vector mass, while the dominant gravitational waveforms remain close to vacuum after time, phase, and amplitude alignment. This contrast highlights the limited imprint of the field on aligned merger-ringdown morphology at these resolutions.
papers.authors: Adrian Ka-Wai Chung

papers.title: Cross-correlating the SPHEREx extragalactic background light with CMB lensing I: theoretical predictions and forecasts
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The near-infrared extragalactic background light (EBL), which SPHEREx maps in 102 spectral channels, holds the emission lines of galaxies on top of a much brighter continuum from the integrated galaxy light (IGL) and the intrahalo light (IHL). Cross-correlating these maps with the lensing of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) isolates the emission that traces the matter, unbiased by uncorrelated foregrounds. The lines face two obstacles. Filtering along the line of sight removes the long radial modes that carry the cross-correlation, and the extragalactic continuum, a signal in its own right, is a correlated foreground for the lines. We forecast the detectability of all EBL components, in a common halo-model framework, for the SPHEREx deep fields and all-sky survey with lensing maps at the sensitivity level of Planck and the Simons Observatory (SO). Without filtering, and with all amplitudes fitted jointly, the cross-correlation with Planck lensing detects the IGL at $9\sigma$ in the deep fields, but not the lines. In the all-sky survey, it measures the IGL and IHL amplitudes to $1.0\%$ and $3\%$ and detects the five lines, fitted as one template, at $4.6\sigma$. With SO lensing, these become $0.6\%$, $1.6\%$ and $7.4\sigma$. In these joint fits, a filter removing radial modes longer than about $600$ Mpc costs every component $90\%$ or more of its signal-to-noise ratio, so the lines are reached by fitting the continuum, not by filtering it. These values assume a known spectral shape of the continuum. Calibrating it with the continuum's auto-spectra keeps the lines at $7.3$--$7.4\sigma$; fitting it from the cross-spectrum alone leaves $1.4$--$2.3\sigma$. The line detections vary by a factor of seven to eleven across line models. The cross-correlation is thus a robust probe of the IGL and a viable route to the emission lines, provided the continuum is modeled across the channels.
papers.authors: Azadeh Moradinezhad Dizgah, Zucheng Gao, Tom Chiesura

papers.title: Cross-correlating the SPHEREx extragalactic background light with CMB lensing II: theoretical predictions confronted with lightcone simulations
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-correlating intensity maps with the lensing of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) rejects the foregrounds and noise that do not trace the dark matter. In the near infrared, the remaining signal combines the integrated galaxy light (IGL), the intrahalo light (IHL) and several emission lines. Accurate modeling of all three is essential to forecast detectability and interpret measurements. We present simulated SPHEREx intensity maps of all three on a lightcone, painted on halos from the Hidden Valley $N$-body simulation, and the CMB-lensing convergence of the same lightcone, over $100\,{\rm deg}^2$ to $z \approx 6$. We assign each halo its lines and continuum by stellar-population synthesis, in two models whose metallicities are fixed or follow its stellar mass. Halo-model predictions from the simulation's luminosity-halo mass relations and measured clustering, without free parameters, match the auto-spectra of the IGL and lines, and their cross-spectra with lensing, across the band: at $2.2\,\mu$m, to within $5\%$ above $\ell \approx 400$ and $7\%$ above $\ell = 200$, respectively. The agreement requires nonlinear clustering: linear theory describes the cross-spectrum of a line up to $\ell \approx 1000$-$1600$ at $2.2\,\mu$m, but fails for the IGL and the convergence at multipoles of a few hundred. With the noise of a SPHEREx deep field and of Simons Observatory lensing, the unfiltered cross-spectra, each component taken alone, reach signal-to-noise ratios of $9$-$21$ for the lines, $20$ for the IGL and $15$ for the IHL. A filter that removes radial modes longer than about $600$ Mpc keeps $62\%$ of the IGL's signal-to-noise and at most $20\%$ of the lines', with fitted amplitudes within about $1\sigma$ of the predictions before and after filtering. The emission model changes a channel's intensity by up to a factor of three, but the line detectability only by tens of percent.
papers.authors: Azadeh Moradinezhad Dizgah, Zucheng Gao

papers.title: FLZ integrability in the 't Hooft model
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the 't Hooft equation describing mesons in large-$N_c$ two-dimensional QCD with arbitrary unequal quark masses. Using its Fredholm formulation and the associated Baxter finite-difference equation, we investigate the relations between spectral determinants and canonical Baxter $Q$-functions. We derive special-point identities for the Baxter solutions by exploiting finite-rank commutator relations of the underlying integral operators. We also determine the spectral residues of the inhomogeneous solutions and obtain exact expressions for eigenfunction normalization factors in terms of values at distinguished complex points. These results establish the unit-residue property of the Baxter expressions entering the Fateev-Lukyanov-Zamolodchikov (FLZ) spectral-determinant identities. As a further application, we prove the nondegeneracy of the meson spectrum for arbitrary unequal quark masses. We further identify a broader class of integral operators exhibiting the same mechanism, which we refer to as FLZ integrability, and illustrate its applicability to the meson spectral problem in Ising field theory. Our approach reveals a connection between the analytic structure of Baxter equations and the theory of completely integrable Fredholm operators.
papers.authors: Alexey Litvinov, Egor Shestopalov, Nikita Slavnov

papers.title: Spectro-Spatial Survey Fusion
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Imaging and spectroscopy constrain complementary information about the same sky but are usually processed separately. We introduce Spectro-Spatial Survey Fusion, a framework that unifies these measurements by fitting a continuous spectral surface-brightness field jointly through each instrument's response. Adapting from Gaussian splatting in computer vision, we represent the field as a sum of adaptive spatial Gaussians, each carrying a spectrum built from a shared, learned dictionary of templates. We demonstrate this on 400 Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) $ugriz$ exposures and 800 fiber spectra across an $84^{\prime}\times84^{\prime}$ region of COSMOS. The joint fit closely reproduces the spatial structure and broad spectral diversity of galaxies, stars, and quasars. For fitted SDSS observations, the summed predicted flux in source-selected pixels agrees with the data to within 2 percent in every band, and 96 percent of fitted spectra agree to within 10 percent in integrated flux. Sparse fiber spectra constrain a dictionary shared by every Gaussian component, so a model spectrum can be queried anywhere in the imaged area, including where no spectrum was fitted. Without refitting, the field predicts withheld SDSS images and spectra, and selected Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) images and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectra, which never enter the fit. The field predicts broad spiral-arm patterns in HSC images of two selected galaxies and DESI continuum shapes for galaxies without a fitted fiber. This framework provides a route to combining surveys so that spatial and spectral information from different observations and instruments can constrain a common representation of the sky.
papers.authors: Georgios N. Vassilakis, Miles Cranmer, Vasily Belokurov

papers.title: A Forecast for Testing the Decreasing $H_0$ Trend in Time-Delay Cosmography
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2019 the H0LiCOW/TDCOSMO collaboration reported a decreasing Hubble constant $H_0$ trend with lens redshift in the flat $\Lambda$CDM model at low statistical significance ($< 2 \sigma$). The signal is expected if physics is missing from the $\Lambda$CDM model in the late universe. In the wake of recent TDCOSMO 2026 results, we revisit the feature. Although the statistical significance of the trend has increased in a like-for-like comparison with earlier studies, propagating mass-sheet transformation (MST) uncertainties reduces the significance to $\sim 1 \sigma$. As a result, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) currently favours a constant $H_0$ over a decreasing $H_0$ in the ratio 2.4:1. Nevertheless, we highlight good agreement on a negative slope with independent observables and forecast that approximately 40 and 90 lenses will be required to substantiate the trend at $\sim 2 \sigma$ and $\sim 3 \sigma$ significance, respectively, if the feature is physical and current uncertainties are representative. Even now, it is evident that the TDCOSMO 2026 $H_0$ constraint $H_0 \approx 71$ km/s/Mpc reflects an average over the lens redshift distribution and is naturally anchored at intermediate lens redshifts.
papers.authors: Shane Brady, Eoin \'O Colg\'ain, M. M. Sheikh-Jabbari

papers.title: Simple Models of Thermal Order in $2+1$ Dimensions
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heating need not destroy order. We show that it persists to arbitrarily high temperatures in simple quantum field theories in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions. In a $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ model of two real scalar fields, a sufficiently negative mixed quartic coupling drives one field to condense, spontaneously breaking its $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry. When coupled to massless Dirac fermions through a Yukawa interaction, this condensate generates a fermion mass, thereby spontaneously breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries. We extend this construction to a $\mathbb Z_2\times O(n)$ scalar model, in which the Mermin-Wagner theorem precludes spontaneous breaking of the continuous $O(n)$ symmetry at finite temperatures. Nevertheless, for $n=2$, a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless superfluid phase persists to arbitrarily high temperatures. In this phase, spatial correlations decay algebraically, with an exponent that approaches zero as the temperature increases. For $n\geq 3$, we uncover a further unexpected feature of these models: the characteristic size of ordered domains grows asymptotically with temperature, revealing an unusual enhancement of spatial correlations upon heating. We establish our results using a controlled high-temperature expansion, with selected findings corroborated by numerical functional renormalization group analysis. The simplicity of the field content in these models provides a promising starting point for exploring experimental realizations of persistent thermal order in thin-film materials.
papers.authors: Michael Smolkin, Lev Yung

papers.title: Structure Constants of Planar N=4 SYM at Any Coupling
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We recast a recent conjecture for structure constants in planar N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory in a separation-of-variables-inspired form suitable for non-perturbative analysis. All state-dependent information enters through the quantum spectral curve. As a showcase, we compute at finite coupling the three-point functions of two half-BPS operators and the spin-two member of the Konishi multiplet. Our results span weak to strong coupling, reproduce the known perturbative and string-theory limits, and are consistent with conformal-bootstrap bounds. We also obtain new six- and seven-loop perturbative coefficients and extract new strong-coupling data from high-precision numerical fits.
papers.authors: Simon Ekhammar, Alessandro Georgoudis, Nikolay Gromov

papers.title: Self-gravitating Lee-Huang-Yang fluids as dark matter halos
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.21911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a model of dark matter halos based on a self-gravitating Bose fluid whose effective equation of state is dominated by Lee-Huang-Yang quantum fluctuations. The model is governed by coupled generalized Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson equations, which incorporate quantum pressure, Lee-Huang-Yang-induced repulsion, and gravitational attraction. By retaining the full quantum pressure, we examine the halo structure from its central region to its asymptotic regime. We first derive the Jeans dispersion relation and analyze how the Lee-Huang-Yang fluctuations alter the gravitational instability criterion and the associated characteristic length and mass scales. We then obtain analytical expressions for the central and large-radius behaviors of the equilibrium solutions. To verify the validity and the performance of the model, we fit the model-predicted curves with a sample of 20 galaxies from the SPARC database and compare the results with those obtained from Navarro-Frenk-White, standard Bose-Einstein condensate, and quantum-droplet dark matter models. We find that the pure-LHY model reproduces a broad range of observed galactic kinematics, yielding reduced $\chi^2$ values and a lower sample average compared to the aforementioned models. These results indicate that the combined effects of quantum pressure, LHY quantum fluctuations and the self-gravity provide additional flexibility in describing both the central and extended outer regions of galactic halos. We also discuss the implications of the inferred halo parameters and emphasize their dependence on the assumed effective equation of state and its microscopic interpretation. The pure-LHY model constitutes an ideal platform for exploring the role of quantum-fluctuation-induced interaction in the formation and structure of dark matter halos.
papers.authors: Abdelaali Boudjemaa

papers.title: Regular/Singular Black Hole Thermodynamics from Renormalised Volume/Area
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the finite mismatch between the holographically and topologically renormalised Euclidean actions of the four-dimensional AdS C-metric. Starting from the relation between Renormalised Volume and the Einstein sector of Conformal Gravity, we separate the regular curvature contribution from the contributions supported on the two conical axes. After introducing the usual Euler normalisation for smooth manifolds, the residual difference between the regular action evaluations is determined by the tension-weighted Euler terms of the renormalised worldsheet area. We identify this difference with the Gauss--Bonnet entropy contribution at the polar conical points of the horizon. The ordinary Euler characteristic remains fixed, while the deficits determine how its curvature representation is divided between regular and singular contributions. At fixed total string tension, the difference of the renormalised worldsheet areas per unit Euclidean time determines the relative tension work, giving a geometric interpretation of the relative thermodynamic length.
papers.authors: Gabriel Arenas-Henriquez, Rodrigo Olea, David Rivera-Betancour

papers.title: Finite-wavelength corrections to dynamical friction in fuzzy dark matter: a causal linear-response approach
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A massive body moving through fuzzy dark matter (FDM) generates a density wake whose gravitational backreaction produces dynamical friction. We investigate how finite-wavelength effects modify this force using causal linear-response theory and the statistical Wigner formulation. For a homogeneous Maxwellian background and general isotropic finite-size perturbers, we derive an analytic representation of the gravitational drag and recover the classical Chandrasekhar result under matched regularization conditions. In the controlled semiclassical regime, the leading finite-wavelength correction is quadratic in $\hbar/m_\chi$ and factorizes into a velocity-dependent function and a ratio of spectral moments characterizing the source structure. Remarkably, this correction reduces the drag magnitude independently of the detailed radial source profile within the adopted Maxwellian model. Gaussian and exponential sources illustrate this result. We further establish a controlled remainder bound and clarify the nonuniform behavior of the point-source limit. These findings identify the physical conditions under which wave effects modify classical dynamical friction.
papers.authors: Yu Wang, Meilin Liu, Haiguang Xu, Shoupan Liu

papers.title: Gravitational waves from cosmological first-order phase transitions with fluctuation-induced friction
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study gravitational-wave production in a cosmological first-order phase transition with fluctuation-induced friction using three-dimensional lattice simulations of two coupled scalar fields. Kinetic and gradient energy in the additional field $s$ accumulates near the expanding bubble walls of $\phi$ and affects their motion. The contribution from $s$ exceeds that from $\phi$ at the spectral peak and has a slope similar to that of the bulk flow model over a finite interval above the peak. In the high-wave-number (UV) direction, $\phi$ dominates and the total spectrum develops a broad feature. For the larger coupling, slowly contracting false vacuum remnants persist long after bubble merger.
papers.authors: Jun-Ye Chen, Dongdong Wei, Zong-Kuan Guo

papers.title: What makes the gravito-thermodynamic arrow of time coincide with that of proper time?
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the pursuit of a geometrical resolution to this important question for the evolution of spherically symmetric perfect fluids in general relativity, we excavated a novel result: the presence of volume distortions and inhomogeneities are, though necessary, but not sufficient for the total gravitational entropy to monotonically increase with proper time. We need a further refinement of the space of distortions and only those that favour shell crossing caustics, causing local flocculations and structure formations, can ensure the alignment. This result will have far reaching consequences for the study of thermodynamical viability of various gravitational collapse and cosmological solutions of Einstein field equations.
papers.authors: Samarjit Chakraborty, Rituparno Goswami

papers.title: Probing Velocity-Dependent WIMP Dark Matter Annihilation in Large-Scale Structure
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The unresolved gamma-ray background (UGRB) provides a promising avenue for probing the cosmological annihilation of weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter through its cross-correlation with large-scale structure (LSS). While most previous studies have assumed a velocity-independent (s-wave) annihilation cross section, many well-motivated particle physics models predict annihilation rates that depend on the relative velocity of dark matter particles. In this work, we develop a generalized halo-model framework to investigate the cosmological signatures of velocity-dependent WIMP annihilation. Parameterizing the velocity-weighted annihilation cross section as $\sigma v_{\rm rel}\propto v_{\rm rel}^{n}$, we consider four representative cases corresponding to Sommerfeld-like (n=-1), s-wave (n=0), p-wave (n=2), and d-wave (n=4) annihilation. We show that velocity dependence modifies not only the overall annihilation emission but also the halo population dominating the signal, leading to distinct effective halo biases, redshift distributions, and angular clustering properties. As a result, different annihilation mechanisms leave characteristic signatures in the UGRB-LSS cross-correlation that cannot be captured by the overall gamma-ray intensity alone. As an illustration of the formalism, we perform a statistical forecast for the cross-correlation between the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) UGRB and the Two Micron All Sky Survey Redshift Survey (2MRS) galaxy catalog and derive the projected sensitivities to the velocity-independent annihilation coefficient for these four annihilation scenarios. Our results demonstrate that cosmological cross-correlations provide a powerful and complementary probe of velocity-dependent dark matter annihilation, offering a new avenue for constraining the particle physics of dark matter through its imprints on large-scale structure.
papers.authors: Wen-Qing Guo

papers.title: Gravitational Light Deflection via Fractional Calculus and Chebyshev Polynomial Approximation
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a fractional-calculus-based framework for evaluating gravitational light deflection in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes. By introducing a suitable transformation of the radial coordinate, the deflection integral is recast into an Abel-type integral equation, from which the associated kernel is reconstructed using fractional integration. The leading singular behaviour near the photon sphere is isolated analytically, and the remaining regular part is approximated by a finite Chebyshev polynomial expansion. This combination retains the correct strong-field behaviour while providing an efficient numerical representation of the deflection integral. We demonstrate the accuracy of the method using the Schwarzschild spacetime as a benchmark and compare the resulting deflection angles with the standard strong-deflection approximation and a two-term weak-deflection expansion. We further apply the method to calculate strong-field lensing observables, including the limiting angular position, angular separation, and relative magnification of relativistic images, for the supermassive black holes Sgr A*. The results show that the proposed approach provides an accurate and flexible means of evaluating gravitational deflection angles across a broad range of closest-approach radii. The framework can be extended to other static, spherically symmetric black-hole geometries, including solutions arising in modified theories of gravity.
papers.authors: Aniruddha Ghosh, Ujjal Debnath

papers.title: Geometric optics for gravitational waves in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity: amplitude birefringence and tensor-scalar mixing on general backgrounds
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the propagation of high-frequency gravitational waves in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity within the geometric optics approximation. In contrast to previous work, we allow for a general background with a nonvanishing scalar field, which enables a covariant treatment of amplitude birefringence. The background scalar gradient introduces third-derivative terms into the linearized field equations. These must be treated as subleading for the linearized system to be free of ghosts, which yields a covariant upper bound on the frequency. Tensor-scalar mixing is induced by the Weyl curvature through the Newman-Penrose scalar $\Psi_0$ along the ray. When the mixing is efficient, the propagation eigenmodes consist of one luminal, one subluminal, and one superluminal mode, and a violation of the ghost-free condition leads to a classical instability. From the transport equations at next-to-leading order, we show that, when the mixing is negligible, the relative amplitude of the two helicities depends only on the scalar-field gradients along the ray at the emission and observation events, independently of the path in between.
papers.authors: Tsutomu Kobayashi

papers.title: Using the 0i Einstein equation to break dark-sector degeneracies
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over the past decade, cosmological observations have started to challenge the $\Lambda$CDM model. If these tensions persist, they immediately raise one fundamental question: what new physics could be responsible for them? More specifically, do these deviations arise from a modification of gravity, from an evolving or clustering dark energy component, or from dark matter properties beyond the cold dark matter paradigm? In this paper we show that, with current methods, any observed deviation can always be attributed to more than one sector, preventing us from determining if the tension is due to gravity, dark energy or dark matter. The main reason is that current tests rely on unobservable quantities. These quantities are then either related to observables by assuming the validity of specific equations, or compared with theoretical predictions computed within a given class of theories. Both approaches inevitably break the model independence of the tests, leading to degeneracies between gravity, dark energy, and dark matter. To overcome this limitation, we construct a set of three tests that rely only on observable quantities and that, when combined, can distinguish between the three sectors. We show that the $0i$ Einstein equation -- which is never tested in standard analyses -- adds crucial information to that provided by the gravitational slip equation and the Euler equation.
papers.authors: Camille Bonvin

papers.title: Non-integrability of open strings via Pohlmeyer reduction
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study integrable and non-integrable boundary conditions for classical strings from the point of view of Pohlmeyer reduction. We first consider the integrable case of strings ending on Y=0 non-maximal giant gravitons. Pohlmeyer reduction of such strings leads to a sine-Gordon model, for which a criterion for boundary integrability was provided by Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov. We confirm that the Pohlmeyer field satisfies this condition. We then turn to the main focus of our work, which is open strings on AdS3. By evaluating the Ghoshal-Zamolodchikov criterion for the corresponding Pohlmeyer-reduced models, we are able to distinguish between integrable and non-integrable cases, in line with expectations from recent analytic and numerical studies. We conclude that Pohlmeyer reduction can provide a useful perspective on open-string non-integrability.
papers.authors: Divania Carelse, Laila Tribelhorn, Konstantinos Zoubos

papers.title: Shadows and Images of Black Holes with Purely Nonlinear Scalarization
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the shadows and radiative images of static, spherically symmetric black holes with purely nonlinear scalarization in Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The quartic exponential coupling supports scalarized backgrounds without a linear tachyonic instability of Schwarzschild black holes. We compare mass and coupling dependences and construct images on radially stable backgrounds using optically thin spherical emission and face-on thin disks. On the sampled radially stable branches, we find smaller shadow radii than those of Schwarzschild black holes at the same mass, with reductions reaching approximately $21.7\%$. The sampled radially unstable branches show much smaller shadow-size deviations. The photon-orbit index, which measures radial instability per unit orbital angle, varies nonmonotonically even when the normalized shadow radius changes monotonically. The index also controls the asymptotic compression of higher-order images, providing information complementary to shadow size. For spherical emission, radial infall produces a darker center relative to the bright ring than static emission. For circular disks, we find that smooth metric variations can create an unstable interval separating two stable regions of timelike circular motion. When the disk occupies the stable region connected to infinity, its inner edge moves outward across this transition, suppressing emission inside the geometric shadow boundary while the normalized shadow radius changes only slightly. Our results show that purely nonlinear scalarization can alter images through both photon propagation and the orbital structure of emitting matter, with the visible features depending on the emission model.
papers.authors: Hao Yang

papers.title: Higher Spin Lagrangians for Black Holes in Arbitrary Dimension
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the classical gravitational multipolar structure of rotating objects studying higher-spin Lagrangians coupled to gravity in arbitrary dimensions $D=d+1$. We first consider fields described by totally symmetric tensors with $s$ indices. At finite spin, the minimal coupling depends on both the spin and spacetime dimension. We show that, in the high-spin limit $s\gg 1$, the minimal multipolar expansion becomes dimension independent and it corresponds to the one which reproduces the Kerr solution in four dimensions. Furthermore, we identify a dimension independent relation among the non-minimal coupling coefficients that allows us to reproduce the Myers-Perry multipolar structure in arbitrary dimensions. We then extend our analysis to Lagrangians involving fields with different Young representations, which are allowed in higher dimensions.
papers.authors: Francesco Campanella

papers.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincar\'e algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.
papers.authors: Zi-Hao Liu, Mei Huang

papers.title: Beyond the point lens: radial structure and the horizon in wave-optics gravitational lensing
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime is sensitive to the structure of the lens beyond its total mass: to its exterior radial profile and, as we show, to the boundary condition at its centre. We develop an analytic framework to compute these effects for a scalar wave, as corrections to the wave lensed by a Newtonian point mass. The corrections are organized in inverse powers of the distance from the lens and computed with dressed radial kernels, which include the Newtonian interaction to all orders and resum the long-range phase that invalidates the Born expansion around the free wave. Retaining wavefront curvature, we find that the scattered wave is not the whole response: an inverse-square deformation changes the direct wave by an equal amount, even when the scattered wave is faint. Steeper terms of the exterior potential lead to short-distance divergences, which signal that the exterior geometry alone does not determine the lensed wave: the missing information is a set of local terms fixed by the inner boundary condition. For a Schwarzschild black hole we determine them by matching to the ingoing solution at the horizon. The horizon enters the amplification factor as an absorptive contact term, which reproduces the horizon-area cross section; it is absent for a non-absorbing lens of the same mass, and cannot be described by the thin-lens diffraction integral. It completes the correction quadratic in the mass, where it appears at the same order as finite-distance optical corrections, and largely cancels against them for an aligned source. Together, these results connect Newtonian dressing, diffraction and inner boundary conditions, in a systematic description of corrections to point-mass gravitational-wave lensing.
papers.authors: Alice Garoffolo, Gianmassimo Tasinato

papers.title: Inflation with an Exponential Power-Law Potential:Analytical Slow-Roll Relations, Branch Dynamics, and Conditional Reheating Matching
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study canonical single-field inflation driven by the potential $V(\phi)=M^4\exp(\phi/M_{\rm Pl})(1+k\phi/M_{\rm Pl})^{-1/k}$ with $k<0$. We retain the canonical Einstein--scalar action and derive analytical relations within the slow-roll approximation. Expressing the local spectra through the logarithmic slope $A=kx/(1+kx)$, with $x=\phi/M_{\rm Pl}$, yields an endpoint-independent consistency relation among the scalar tilt, tensor ratio, and running at their stated approximation orders. On the negative-field branch, an exact phase-space argument shows that an initially downhill, inflationary hilltop trajectory cannot end inflation within the bare single-field model. We specify the endpoint as a phenomenological input and use a Lambert-$W$ solution of the slow-roll e-fold integral. Tables and figures illustrate the fixed choice $x_e=-2$ and must be interpreted conditionally on a completion that implements this endpoint and preserves the adiabatic spectrum. The reheating-matching relation uses explicit scale and thermal conventions and imposes both endpoint energy bounds and nonnegative reheating duration. The observational comparison uses published marginalized intervals rather than reconstructed joint posteriors. These results establish local analytical structure and conditional numerical benchmarks. A complete exit mechanism, a unique reheating equation of state, and precision spectral predictions remain unestablished.
papers.authors: Feyzollah Younesizadeh, Younes Younesizadeh, Wen-Xiang Chen

papers.title: Spectral recurrences and maximal analyticity: cosmological correlators at one and two loops
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a method for computing de Sitter boundary correlators based on the maximal analyticity of the two-point function and differential--difference equations satisfied by Schwinger--Keldysh diagrams. The vertex integrations are analytically continued through the relevant de Sitter tuboids onto purely imaginary Lobachevskij cycles. Taking the Mehler--Fock transform of the invariant bubble kernels on these Riemannian cycles converts their differential--difference equations into algebraic recurrences in the spectral parameter. The mixed-branch kernel obeys a homogeneous recurrence, whereas the chronological and antichronological kernels satisfy sourced recurrences whose local terms are determined by dimensionally continued tadpoles. We solve these recurrences, constructing explicit particular solutions in terms of generalised hypergeometric functions and identifying the analytic conditions selecting their physical completion. Attachment to the external boundary points then yields an intrinsic spectral representation and a complete solution of the boundary in--in diagrams considered here. Our method is fully coordinate-independent. Specialising to a Poincar\'e chart readily gives expressions that can be compared directly with those obtained by the standard coordinate-dependent approach. Composing two or more bubbles yields a multi-loop chain whose spectral multiplier is determined by the one-loop building blocks and the sum over intermediate Schwinger--Keldysh branches.
papers.authors: Bruce A. Bassett, Sergio L. Cacciatori, Ugo Moschella

papers.title: Fluid/Gravity Correspondence in 3d Flat Gravity with Non-Compact Boundaries
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study 3d flat gravity on a restricted phase space with a non-compact spatial boundary. The charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras, which a fluid/gravity dictionary maps to the stress tensor of a two-dimensional conformal fluid, with energy bounded below by the momentum. On the line, finiteness of the charges selects integrable, square-integrable currents, and the global data are carried by the scattering variables of a Schr\"odinger operator rather than by a monodromy. We analyze Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like boundary conditions; the latter give independently propagating chiral kinks associated with the reflectionless P\"oschl-Teller operator. Both admit first-law relations. We outline the quantization as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states. Retaining the radial dependence, the quasi-local stress tensor obeys an exact, non-perturbative flow of square-root $T\bar T$ type, which integrates to a finite boost in the radial position.
papers.authors: H. Adami, R. Esp\'indola, K. Lara, A. Latifi

papers.title: Effects of QCD Equation of State on Cosmological Parameters and Stochastic Gravitational-Waves Spectrum
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic evolution of the early Universe across the QCD crossover and up to the electroweak (EW) scale, emphasizing the systematic impact of the QCD equation of state (EoS) and electroweak degrees of freedom on thermodynamic variables, cosmological parameters, and gravitational-wave observables. Using the HotQCD EoS as a baseline, we employ Gaussian Process (GP) regression to generate ensembles of 1000 thermodynamically consistent EoS samples, each extrapolated to high temperatures with and without EW contributions. For each ensemble, we solve the Friedmann equations to obtain the expansion history and compute gravitational-wave (GW) observables, including the instantaneous spectral tilt $n_{gw}(f)$ and the normalized GW energy density $\Omega_{gw}(f)/\Omega_{gw}^{\rm rad}$. We find that including the EW sector is the dominant effect across all observables, outweighing differences among QCD baseline models that share the same lattice calibration. In particular, EW contributions drive the EoS toward the radiation-dominated limit earlier, reduce excursions of the speed of sound toward the causality bound, suppress transient fluctuations in the Hubble and kinematic parameters near $t \sim 10^{-5}$ s, and qualitatively change the GW spectrum from a strongly frequency-dependent signal to a flat, suppressed plateau. These results demonstrate that accurate modeling of the electroweak sector is essential for an unbiased extraction of QCD-era physics from the stochastic gravitational-wave background.
papers.authors: Andr\'e V. Giannini, Victor P. Gon\c{c}alves, Samuel M. Sanches Jr

papers.title: Gravitational Waves Population Study for Testing Kerr Hypothesis: Are Non-Kerr Deformations Universal or Source-Dependent?
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravitational-wave observations of binary black hole mergers can test the Kerr black hole hypothesis in the strong-field and dynamical regime. In our previous works, we constrained the deformation parameters $\alpha_{13}$ and $\epsilon_3$ of the Johannsen metric using individual inspiral-dominated events from GWTC-3 and GWTC-4 and found no evidence of deviations from the Kerr solution. Here we combine 17 of these events to test whether black holes are Kerr, share a common non-zero deformation, or have deformations that vary from source to source. We first estimate the Savage--Dickey Bayes factor of each event, and we test how it depends on the prior range and on the removal of single events. We then combine the event likelihoods assuming a universal deformation, yielding a tighter joint constraint. Next, we perform a simple hierarchical analysis by assuming that the event-level deformation parameters are drawn from a population with mean $\mu$ and intrinsic scatter $\sigma$. A universal deformation is constrained to $\alpha_{13}=-0.01^{+0.14}_{-0.12}$ and $\epsilon_3=0.06^{+0.59}_{-0.54}$. The means from the population are consistent with zero for both parameters, and the scatter is not resolved by the current data. Our results are consistent with the Kerr hypothesis, but they cannot yet distinguish a shared deformation from a source-dependent one.
papers.authors: Debtroy Das, Swarnim Shashank, Cosimo Bambi, Yi-Ming Hu

papers.title: The additive ambiguity of gravitational entropy fixed by the topology of the horizon
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In quantum gravity the algebra of observables of a subregion is of type III$_1$ at leading order in the semiclassical expansion, and it becomes of type II once the gravitational constraint is imposed. Hence generalized entropy acquires a trace, however it is defined only up to an additive constant. In this work we argue that in four-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity this constant is the Gauss--Bonnet contribution to the Wald entropy, and that it is carried by the normalization of the trace and not by the state. In particular, the conical expansion of the Gauss--Bonnet density is exactly linear in the deficit angle, and on smooth squashed cones it reduces to the intrinsic curvature of the cut, so that the term is a constant on every smooth cross-section and carries no boost energy. Its Noether charge is invariant under all deformations within a topological sector and central in any algebra that preserves the sector, and thus a state-independent constant on such an algebra can only rescale the trace. Additionally, when the boundary of the subregion is completed as the Euler action requires, the Gauss--Bonnet term does not contribute to the presymplectic form, the crossed product is inherited from Einstein gravity, and the constant is the Euler number of the excised Euclidean tip. We state the hypotheses, we weaken factoriality to a central decomposition, and we illustrate the mechanism in Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity and in topological black holes in anti-de Sitter space, where the topological weight displaces the Hawking--Page temperature and a black-hole merger shifts the coarse-grained boundary entropy by a state-independent amount.
papers.authors: Stylianos A. Tsilioukas

papers.title: Toric Calabi-Yau orientifolds: constructions, fixed loci and O-plane charges
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review the systematic construction of toric orientifold Calabi-Yau threefolds through divisor exchanges and coordinate reflections. We relate the homogeneous-coordinate and lattice descriptions and explain the computation of fixed loci and the geometric data entering Hodge splittings and tadpole conditions. Our triangulation-wise analysis identifies multiple compatible involutions on a single triangulation and tracks their realisations across different triangulations, revealing the orientifold structure within and across toric phases. We complement this review with new calculations and explicit examples that refine the fixed-locus geometry and the associated orientifold charge data. The examples also identify coordinate representatives of the identity and invariant hypersurface families with unavoidable singularities. These results support an ongoing update of the orientifold catalogue and provide geometric input for D-brane configurations, flux compactifications and moduli stabilisation.
papers.authors: Xu Cao, Xin Gao

papers.title: Quantum phase transition and superselection sectors in two-color one-flavor matrix QCD at weak coupling
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We numerically investigate the weak-coupling (small $g$) regime of the matrix model of $SU(2)$ gauge theory coupled to one flavor of massless fundamental quarks. The theory possesses a global Pauli-G\"ursey $SU(2)_B$ symmetry, which organizes physical states of spin $J$ into sectors labelled by its representation $B$. We find localization-delocalization quantum phase transitions (QPTs) in multiple $(B,J)$ sectors at sector-dependent critical couplings $g_\ast^{BJ}$. Direct evaluation of the localization probability reveals that the ground states are predominantly localized near $A_i=0$ for $g<g_\ast^{BJ}$, but become almost entirely expelled from this region for $g>g_*^{BJ}$. The QPTs in different sectors exhibit distinct features, and we establish that quark-glue interactions are essential for these transitions. The transitions are singular: the ground state expectation value of $\text{Tr}(A_iA_i)$ remains finite for $g< g_\ast^{BJ}$, whereas it diverges as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above. We show that the two limiting ground states on either side of $g_\ast^{BJ}$ belong to distinct superselection sectors. Furthermore, as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above, the ground state localizes on a submanifold (of codimension 2) of the gauge configuration space, with the spin and color of its glue components becoming locked.
papers.authors: Nirmalendu Acharyya, Arkajyoti Bandyopadhyay, Parthsarathi Kondapure, Sachindeo Vaidya

papers.title: 5d $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ S-folds, quotient curves, and isogenies
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct Seiberg--Witten curves for the $\mathbb{Z}_3$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$, and $\mathbb{Z}_6$ S-folds of 5d rank-1 superconformal theories. Compared with the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ case arXiv:2611.09804, $\mathbb{Z}_{3,4,6}$ S-folds require stronger constraints on the mass parameters. We provide a systematic procedure of realizing the S-foldings at the mirror curve level. We obtain the same elliptic curve families by specializing the complexified mass parameters of the rank-1 $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$ theories, with holonomies motivated by the 7-brane insertions required by the S-fold prescription. The two constructions agree in Weierstrass form. The families with continuous mass deformations organize into characters of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{g}_2$, consistently with their singular fibers. Finally, we discuss that the Seiberg--Witten curves for $\mathbb{Z}_n$ S-folds can be obtained through cyclic $n$-isogenies, which may provide a uniform quotient curve description of rank-1 S-folds.
papers.authors: Sung-Soo Kim, Song Liu, Mudassar Sabir, Futoshi Yagi

papers.title: Shell crossing and the dynamical formation of thin shells in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that shell crossing in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust in spherical symmetry can be understood as dynamical formation of a thin shell of dust. More precisely, we consider the spherically symmetric Einstein-dust system in double null coordinates (E-d), for which first singularities with area radius bounded away from zero are known as 'shell crossing' singularities. We show that there exists a weak solution of (E-d), in which a thin shell of dust forms, extending beyond any 'non-degenerate' first shell crossing singularity of a smooth 'collapsing' solution of (E-d). This local extension is unique in the class of piecewise smooth solutions of (E-d) satisfying a 'determinism condition'. We then consider the physical problem of smooth data for (E-d) on an initial hypersurface diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$, containing a collapsing dust cloud. We show that, for generic such initial data, there exists a maximal globally hyperbolic piecewise smooth development satisfying a 'propagation condition' (stronger than the determinism condition). The development may contain an arbitrary (finite) number of thin shells which can moreover merge. All shell crossing singularities are 'resolved' and the area radius extends continuously to zero at any first singularity of the maximal development. We note that, for an open set of initial data in the smooth topology, as shown by Christodoulou, a Cauchy horizon emanates from a central 'shell-focussing' singularity.
papers.authors: Matt Smith

papers.title: Strange-Metal Magnetotransport without a Strange-Metal Ground State
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strange metals display a linear-in-temperature resistivity, $\rho_{xx}\sim T$, and a quadratic inverse Hall angle, $\cot\Theta_H\sim T^2$. These seemingly universal laws are often attributed to quantum criticality, yet no controlled theory realizes both at an asymptotic zero-temperature fixed point, and experimentally they persist only over finite temperature windows. Here, we show that these properties can arise from an intermediate critical regime that does not govern the ground state. Using a minimal class of holographic models, we construct a fully backreacted realization of both scalings, which appear within a finite temperature window controlled by an emergent intermediate scaling geometry. The window is bounded by relevant deformations of the corresponding fixed point: momentum relaxation sets the upper edge, while the magnetic field $B$ closes it from below at $T_{\min}\sim B^{2/3}$, up to logarithmic corrections. At $T_{\min}$, strange-metal transport, the scaling geometry, and critical thermodynamics break down together. Our results point to intermediate criticality as a distinct route to strange-metal transport, and suggest that it can be identified by the simultaneous breakdown of transport and thermodynamic scaling under a magnetic field.
papers.authors: Yongjun Ahn, Matteo Baggioli, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Keun-Young Kim

papers.title: \texttt{StochAXtic}: a JAX-Accelerated, End-to-End Differentiable Framework for Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds from Compact Binary Populations
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.22999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present \texttt{StochAXtic}, a package for computing the dimensionless energy density spectrum $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ of the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by compact binary coalescences. Rather than sampling binary populations via Monte Carlo, \texttt{StochAXtic} exploits the \emph{scale invariance} of the waveforms: at fixed mass ratio, spins and tidal deformabilities, the waveform depends on the total mass only through the dimensionless combination $Mf$. This allows all computationally expensive waveform evaluations using \texttt{LALSuite} to be performed once and stored in a population-independent lookup table. The subsequent integrals over mass and redshift can then be recast as convolutions and evaluated efficiently using fast Fourier transforms. We further employ truncated singular value decomposition to compress the lookup table, reducing both computational cost and memory requirements. Once the table has been computed and cached, \texttt{StochAXtic} evaluates $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ in a few milliseconds, achieving a relative numerical error below $10^{-3}$ at frequencies up to $1$ kHz.
